```{r setup, include=FALSE}



# --- Load ALL necessary libraries ---
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(DESeq2)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(indicspecies)
library(FSA) # For Dunn's Test
library(tidyverse) # For data manipulation

# --- Read OTU Table ---
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")


otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]


rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group 


otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)


otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
# --- Read and Process Taxonomy ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, quote = "")
taxonomy_clean <- lapply(strsplit(tax_raw$Taxonomy, ";"), function(x) {
    x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)|\\\"", "", x[nchar(x) > 0]); trimws(x)
})
max_ranks <- 7; taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, `length<-`, max_ranks))
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- tax_raw$OTU
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))

# --- Read and Process NEW Metadata (kohlerrr.design) ---
metadata <- read.table("kohler.design.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
colnames(metadata)[2:3] <- c("SampleType", "Age")
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$SampleID
metadata <- metadata[, -1] 
metadata$SampleType <- factor(metadata$SampleType)
metadata$Feed <- factor(metadata$Feed)
sample_data_obj <- sample_data(metadata)
```

```{r phyloseq-object}

# Read OTU table
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")

# Set rownames of the matrix (Taxa) before transposing
# The original row names are NOT needed as they are just row numbers.

# Extract only the count data columns (from column 4 onwards)
otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]

# CRITICAL: Set the row names of the matrix (these are the sample IDs)
# This MUST be done before transposing
rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group 

# Transpose the matrix so OTUs are rows and Samples are columns
# Now, otu_mat has OTUs as rows (OTU IDs) and Samples as columns (Sample IDs)
otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

# Create phyloseq OTU table
# taxa_are_rows = TRUE is correct after the transpose
otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# Check the result
head(otu_tab)
# Read and Process Taxonomy

```

```{r}
# --- 1. Read the taxonomy file ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", 
                      sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "")

# --- 2. Extract taxonomy strings and OTU IDs ---
taxonomy_strings <- tax_raw$Taxonomy
names(taxonomy_strings) <- tax_raw$OTU

# --- 3. Split taxonomy strings by ';' and clean ---
taxonomy_clean <- strsplit(taxonomy_strings, ";")

taxonomy_clean <- lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  x <- x[nchar(x) > 0]                # Remove empty strings
  x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)", "", x)       # Remove confidence scores in parentheses
  x <- gsub('\\"', '', x)              # Remove escaped quotes
  trimws(x)                           # Trim whitespace
})

# --- 4. Pad each taxonomy vector to length 7 (Kingdom to Species) ---
max_ranks <- 7
taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  length(x) <- max_ranks  # pad with NAs if needed
  x
}))

# --- 5. Assign column and row names ---
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- names(taxonomy_strings)

# --- 6. Create tax_table object for phyloseq ---
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))

# --- Optional: Check the result ---
head(tax_tab)
```


```{r metadata-read-final}

# Load the phyloseq package
library(phyloseq)

# 1. Read the design file using the ROBUST separator sep=""
# sep="" tells R to use one or more whitespace characters (tabs/spaces) as a delimiter.
metadata <- read.table("Kohler.design", header = TRUE, sep = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Check the column names to verify the read
# print(colnames(metadata)) 

# 2. Rename columns for clarity and consistency (5 columns should be read now)
# Index 2: Mother -> MotherID
colnames(metadata)[2] <- "MotherID"

# Index 5: Feed -> FeedStatus
colnames(metadata)[5] <- "FeedStatus" 

# 3. Set rownames using the SampleID
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$SampleID

# 4. Prepare for phyloseq
metadata <- metadata[, -1] # Remove the redundant SampleID column

# 5. Ensure categorical variables are factors
metadata$Age <- factor(metadata$Age)
metadata$SampleType <- factor(metadata$SampleType)
metadata$FeedStatus <- factor(metadata$FeedStatus)
metadata$MotherID <- factor(metadata$MotherID)

# 6. Create the phyloseq 'sample_data' object
sample_data_obj <- sample_data(metadata)

head(sample_data_obj)
```

```{r phyloseq-object-final}

# Load necessary library
library(phyloseq)

# --- Ensure components are named for pruning ---

# Get sample names from the metadata object (which is assumed to be correct now)
meta_samples <- sample_names(sample_data_obj)

# --- Prune OTU and Tax tables to match metadata ---
# This step ensures that all components have identical sample names and counts.
otu_tab_pruned <- prune_samples(meta_samples, otu_tab)
tax_tab_pruned <- prune_taxa(taxa_names(otu_tab_pruned), tax_tab)

# --- Combine components ---
# Note: If you have a phylogenetic tree object (e.g., 'tree_obj'), add it here.
physeq <- phyloseq(otu_tab_pruned, tax_tab_pruned, sample_data_obj)

# Check the final object
print(physeq)
```

```{r alpha-diversity}

# Calculate alpha diversity
alpha_diversity <- estimate_richness(physeq, measures = c("Shannon", "Simpson"))

# Plot alpha diversity
plot_richness(physeq, x = "SampleType", measures = c("Shannon", "Simpson")) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(fill = SampleType)) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r beta-diversity}
# Calculate distance matrix
dist_matrix <- phyloseq::distance(physeq, method = "bray")
# Perform ordination
ord <- ordinate(physeq, method = "NMDS", distance = "bray")

# Plot ordination
plot_ordination(physeq, ord, color = "SampleType") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  theme_minimal()

```

```{r differential-abundance}
# Convert to DESeq2 object
dds <- phyloseq_to_deseq2(physeq, ~ SampleType)

# Run DESeq2
dds <- DESeq(dds)

# Results
res <- results(dds)
```

```{r indicator-species}
# Run indicator species analysis
indval_result <- multipatt(t(as(otu_table(physeq), "matrix")), metadata$SampleType, func = "indval")
summary(indval_result)
```
